# Noisemaker

Noisemaker is an open source shader framework for humans and coding agents.
Use it to build expressive, extensible visual tools for web, desktop, and mobile.
It supports:

- WebGL2 and WebGPU.
- The high-level Polymorphic DSL.
- Declarative effect definitions.
- Portable effect packages.
- External media/audio/MIDI inputs.
- Shader bundles distributed through a CDN.

Use this file as the short public map. For a fuller agent-oriented overview, read `/llms-full.txt`.

## Primary Links

- [Homepage](https://noisemaker.app/): Product overview and demos.
- [Shader demo](https://noisemaker.app/demo/shaders/): Interactive effect browser and DSL editor.
- [Docs](https://docs.noisemaker.app/): In-house documentation root.
- [Source](https://github.com/noisefactorllc/noisemaker): Noisemaker repository.

## Core Documentation

- [Shader integration](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/integration/): Embedding `CanvasRenderer` from the CDN or local bundles.
- [Shader specs](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/specs/): Effect format, Polymorphic DSL, pipeline, compiler, and effect reference.
- [Pipeline spec](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/pipeline/): DSL to render graph, resource allocation, and GPU dispatch.
- [Language spec](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/language/): Polymorphic DSL syntax and semantics.
- [Effect definition spec](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/effects/): Effect definitions, namespaces, tags, globals, textures, and passes.
- [Scene graph spec](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/scene/): `scene()` programs: camera, lights, meshes, volumes, materials, animation, host control, hosting requirements.
- [Deferred renderer spec](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/deferred-rendering/): How scenes are drawn: G-buffer, lighting model, SSAO, reflections, probe, tonemap, backend parity.

## Experimental features

These are new features that exist to seed the Noisemaker 2.x feature set. Node names, keywords, defaults, argument shapes, and rendered output may all change without a deprecation period. There is no flag to turn them on.

- **The scene vocabulary** (`scene`): `scene()` adds a third dimension to the Polymorphic DSL. A scene program describes a camera, lights, and a hierarchy of meshes and volumes with PBR materials. Current limits: One `scene()` per program, one `environment()`. Primitives only; no loaded models inside `scene()`. The camera cannot be animated from the DSL; a light's position and direction cannot either. A program re-emitted from its parsed form comes back with the whole `scene()` on one line and its interior comments removed. [Documentation](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/scene/)
- **The deferred renderer** (`scene.deferred`): The renderer that draws `scene()` programs. It fills a G-buffer from the mesh hierarchy, lights it once in screen space with a Cook-Torrance BRDF, adds ambient occlusion and reflections, tonemaps, and presents into a texture the 2D pipeline then treats as an ordinary source. Current limits: One `reflector()` per scene. No cast shadows. [Documentation](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/deferred-rendering/)
- **Volume nodes** (`scene.volume`): `volume()` places a density volume in the scene graph. Its positional argument is one of the pipeline's eight volume surfaces, so a 3D program that fills an atlas with `write3d()` becomes a node beside the meshes rather than a separate fullscreen marcher with its own camera and lights. Current limits: `volume()` samples a fixed 64-cube atlas. [Documentation](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/scene/#shader-scene-volumes)
- **External inputs in scenes** (`scene.inputs`): Transform components and light intensity accept `midi()` for a MIDI channel and `audio()` for a frequency band, in place of numbers. Current limits: Descriptors on `pos`, `scale` and `intensity` produce `0..1`. [Documentation](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/scene/#shader-scene-animation)
- **Cubemap export of scenes** (`scene.cubemapExport`): A `scene()` program exports a cubemap through the same `renderCubemap()` API as a cubemap-renderer program. Current limits: Faces are never tiled, and a configured reflection probe is captured once for the first face and frozen for the rest. A second export started before the first settles is rejected. [Documentation](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/scene/#shader-scene-cubemap-export)
- **Tiled export of scenes** (`scene.tiledExport`): `setTileRegion` tiles a scene by restricting the camera to the tile's sub-frustum. Current limits: SSAO can seam within its kernel's projected reach, and local screen-space reflections cannot be tiled at all. The reflection probe is never tiled. [Documentation](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/scene/#shader-scene-tiled-export)
- **glTF loading** (`gltf`): `loadGLTFFromURL()` and `loadGLTFFromString()` load glTF and GLB mesh files. Each takes the target surface as its second argument, defaulting to `mesh0`. Current limits: Loaded models cannot be placed in a `scene()`. [Documentation](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/language/#shader-language-gltf)
- **Mixed argument order** (`lang.mixedArguments`): Keywords claim their own parameter slots by name, wherever they appear in the call. The positionals are then bound in source order to the slots no keyword claimed, left to right. [Documentation](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/language/#shader-language-mixed-arguments)
- **Object literals** (`lang.objectLiteral`): `{ key: value }` is an expression. Current limits: No call takes an object as a value yet. [Documentation](https://docs.noisemaker.app/shaders/language/#shader-language-object-literals)

<!-- stability:end experimental-features -->

## Agent Tooling

For the roles and control paths of the Noise Factor apps, including
Timeline, start from the [platform guide](https://noisefactor.io/llms.txt).

Start with the "Portable effect authoring" section of [llms-full.txt](https://noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt) for host-independent discovery, typed bindings, paired shaders, looping, rendered checks and export round trips.

The [effect manifest](https://shaders.noisedeck.app/1/effects/manifest.json) lists every effect as `namespace/name`. Each effect's `help.md` gives its parameters with their types, defaults and ranges, as plain text: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noisefactorllc/noisemaker/v<version>/shaders/effects/<namespace>/<name>/help.md`, where `<version>` is the `version` in https://shaders.noisedeck.app/1/deployment-meta.json, the engine that the apps run.

For app control, read the hosting application's own guide. Its guide adds
shader-craft and reference-video workflows.

- [shade-mcp](https://github.com/noisefactorllc/shade-mcp): MCP server for effect search, source search, compile, render, metrics, parity, and structure checks.
- [portable](https://github.com/noisefactorllc/portable): Portable effect package format with definition JSON, help docs, GLSL, WGSL, and viewer.

## Demos

- [Noisedeck.app](https://noisedeck.app): A comprehensive UI that fully exercises Noisemaker.
- [Layers](https://layers.noisefactor.io): A non-destructive layer-based image and video clip editor built on Noisemaker.
- [Demos](https://demos.noisemaker.app): Noisemaker demos, ports, and source adapters.

## Notes For Agents

- Polymorphic DSL is not GLSL or WGSL.
- Effect paths such as `synth/noise` are not DSL function calls.
- Effects should use internal textures for private state. User surfaces `o0` through `o7` belong to the composition graph.
- Custom integrations can use `registerNamespace()` and the `user` namespace.
- Portable effects use `definition.json`, `help.md`, GLSL, WGSL, and the Noisemaker DSL.
- Validate generated shader work:

  1. Compile the shaders.
  2. Render the output.
  3. Check the metrics.
  4. Test WebGL2/WebGPU parity when both backends matter.
